provenance: LLM-backend-derived (this session, no API key) + deterministic-checked — NOT a ship typology config. build_rec follows the cover×data matrix (build_rec_category); every indicator's flag is quote-grounded (verbatim) in the source md within the red-flag region (Phase 16). Coverage/data values are ILLUSTRATIVE (vision demo). FinCEN Alert, public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).

indicators.flag:
Transactions	related	to	payments	for	defense	or	dual-use	products	from	a	company
incorporated	after	February	24,	2022,	and	based	in	a	non-GECC	country.
indicators.rationale: The bank sees the payment and counterparty country, but tying a payment to defense/dual-use goods and confirming the counterparty's incorporation date needs trade-document and external registry enrichment.

indicators.flag:
A	new	customer	whose	line	of	business	is	in	trade	of	products	associated	with	the	nine	HS
codes,	is	based	in	a	non-GECC	country,	and	was	incorporated	after	February	24,	2022.
indicators.rationale: Resolving a new customer's HS-code product line and post-Feb-2022 incorporation depends on external corporate-registry and goods-classification data the bank does not hold at onboarding.

indicators.flag:
An	existing	customer	who	did	not	receive	exports	associated	with	the	nine	HS	codes	prior	to
February	24,	2022,	but	who	is	receiving	such	items	now.
indicators.rationale: The bank holds the customer's full trade-payment history, so a first-appearance of nine-HS-code activity after a fixed cutoff date is directly computable from internal data.

build_logic.logic: For each customer, compute the set of the nine high-priority HS codes seen in trade payments before 2022-02-24; flag when one or more of those HS codes appears in the current window with no pre-cutoff history.
build_logic.source: trade-finance payment records + commercial-invoice HS-code tags
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → trade-finance compliance review gate

indicators.flag:
An	existing	customer,	based	outside	the	United	States,	received	exports	associated	with	one	or
more	of	the	nine	HS	codes	prior	to	February	24,	2022,	and	requested	or	received	a	significant
increase	in	exports	with	those	same	codes	thereafter.
indicators.rationale: A post-cutoff volume spike against a customer's own pre-cutoff baseline for the same HS codes is a windowed comparison fully derivable from internal trade-payment history.

build_logic.logic: For non-US customers with pre-2022-02-24 activity in any of the nine HS codes, compute the ratio of current-window export volume to the pre-cutoff baseline for those same codes; flag when the ratio exceeds a configurable spike threshold.
build_logic.source: trade-finance payment records with HS-code tags + customer domicile from KYC
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → trade-finance compliance review gate

indicators.flag:
A	customer	lacks	or	refuses	to	provide	details	to	banks,	shippers,	or	third	parties,	including
about	end	users,	intended	end-use,	or	company	ownership.
indicators.rationale: Refusal-to-provide is partly captured in KYC/EDD case notes but end-user and ownership gaps need document-request workflow and external attribution to fully assess.

indicators.flag:
Transactions	involving	smaller-volume	payments	from	the	same	end	user’s	foreign	bank
account	to	multiple,	similar	suppliers	of	dual-use	products.
indicators.rationale: Fan-out of small payments from one foreign account to many similar suppliers is a structuring-style graph pattern computable from wire and payment data the bank already processes.

build_logic.logic: Aggregate outbound payments by source foreign bank account over the window; flag accounts dispersing below-threshold payments to a count of distinct, business-similar suppliers above a configurable fan-out threshold.
build_logic.source: wire and correspondent-banking payment records + supplier MCC/line-of-business tags
build_logic.route: Tier-1 alert → AML transaction-monitoring review gate

indicators.flag:
Parties	to	transactions	listed	as	ultimate	consignees	or	listed	in	the	“consign	to”	field	do	not
typically	engage	in	business	consistent	with	consuming	or	otherwise	using	commodities	(e.g.,
other	financial	institutions,	mail	centers,	or	logistics	companies).
indicators.rationale: The consignee fields live on trade documents the bank handles but classifying whether the consignee's business is consistent with consuming the goods needs document parsing and entity-type enrichment.

indicators.flag: The	customer	is	significantly	overpaying	for	a	commodity	based	on	known	market	prices.
indicators.rationale: The invoiced price is in the trade-payment record, but detecting significant overpayment requires an external market-price reference for the commodity to benchmark against.

indicators.flag:
The	customer	or	its	address	is	similar	to	one	of	the	parties	on	a	proscribed	parties	list,	such	as	the
BIS	Entity	List,	the	SDN	List,	or	the	U.S.	Department	of	State’s	Statutorily	Debarred	Parties	List.33
indicators.rationale: Name and address fuzzy-matching against the SDN, BIS Entity, and debarred-parties lists is standard sanctions-screening that a mid-size US bank already runs at onboarding and on transactions.
